stories.headline: OpenAI Cuts Off Cursor After SpaceX Acquisition, Ending Access November 12
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI invoked a change-of-control clause to terminate Cursor model access effective November 12, 2026, citing distrust of SpaceX after Elon Musk companies repeatedly violated its contracts and terms of service.
stories.article_excerpt: OpenAI has told Elon Musk it is taking its models back. On August 28, 2026, the company notified SpaceX that Cursor access ends.

pull_quote.text: Cursor was one of the very first users of OpenAI, we have worked closely with their team for years, and we have trusted their platform to be neutral infrastructure for our business.

stories.headline: Anthropic Doubles Down on Cursor With Higher Claude Limits as OpenAI Walks Away
stories.key_takeaway: Anthropic reaffirmed and expanded its Cursor partnership within hours of the OpenAI cutoff notice, betting that its model-as-infrastructure business cannot afford to abandon its largest third-party developer channel.
stories.article_excerpt: Anthropic needed about ninety minutes to answer the biggest question in developer tooling this week, and it answered with compute.

pull_quote.text: Cursor has been a trusted partner of Anthropic since Sonnet 3.5. We will continue to increase compute to support Claude models in Cursor and are excited for what comes next with them at SpaceX.
pull_quote.role: Co-founder and Chief Compute Officer, Anthropic

stories.headline: Inside Project OT: How Meta Plan to Cut Teams 60% and Replace Them With Agents Collapsed
stories.key_takeaway: Meta built an entire 60% headcount reduction plan around AI agents, then killed the second layoff wave when internal data showed agents produced far more code but only marginally more shipped features and a sharp rise in incidents.
stories.article_excerpt: Project OT had a code name, a retreat, a playbook, and a date on the calendar. What it did not have was technology that worked.

pull_quote.text: The trajectory of the agentic development over at least the last four months has not really accelerated in the way that we expected.

stories.headline: AWS Opens 900+ Cloud and AI Courses to Students in $500M Skills Push
stories.key_takeaway: AWS is handing verified university students a $579 package of premium training, credits and a certification voucher under a $500 million banner, a distribution play that lands exactly as AI squeezes entry-level hiring.
stories.article_excerpt: AWS is giving away a $449-a-year training subscription to anyone who can prove they are enrolled at a university.

pull_quote.text: It reminds me of why I do this work, and that the students I meet today may well become our customers and collaborators tomorrow.

data_points.label: Young Romanians citing AI job squeeze

stories.headline: Europe Grids Hit Their Limit as Speculative Data Centre Projects Clog the Queue
stories.key_takeaway: Electricity, not compute or capital, has become the binding constraint on Europe AI buildout, and regulators from London to Utrecht are now rationing grid access rather than expanding it.
stories.article_excerpt: Britain energy regulator published a figure that reframes the entire debate about AI infrastructure in Europe.

pull_quote.text: Britain electricity demand connections queue has more than tripled in size in less than a year, and consumers should not bear the risks created by speculative projects taking up space in the system.
pull_quote.role: Director for Energy System Design and Development, Ofgem

data_points.label: Grid wait times in European hubs

stories.headline: MiniMax Pushes M3 to General Availability, Adding a 428B MoE to the Open-Weight Flood
stories.key_takeaway: MiniMax 428B-parameter M3 is the strongest open-weight model on independent indices, but it arrived inside a nine-day wave of cheaper rivals that turned million-token context and native multimodality into commodity features.
stories.article_excerpt: MiniMax spent the summer doing what Chinese AI labs now treat as routine: ship a frontier-class model behind an API, then open it.

pull_quote.text: The model is now the cheap part, and the expensive part is everything around it: effort settings, cache hit rate, provider choice and retry behaviour.

data_points.label: Price per million in / out tokens

stories.headline: ChatGPT Temporary Chats Get Memory, Plugins and a Save Button
stories.key_takeaway: OpenAI August 27 update lets ChatGPT temporary chats read existing memories, custom instructions and plugins if the user opts in, and lets any temporary chat be saved into permanent history.
stories.article_excerpt: For two years ChatGPT Temporary Chat behaved like a burner phone: nothing came in, nothing went out, nothing stayed.

pull_quote.text: This fundamentally conflicts with the privacy commitments we have made to our users. It abandons long-standing privacy norms and weakens privacy protections.

data_points.label: Ship date for the new controls
Chat logs ordered produced in NYT case

stories.headline: The Producers Turned Detectives: Inside the Hunt for AI-Generated Songs on Streaming
stories.key_takeaway: With AI tracks now exceeding half of Deezer daily uploads and platform labeling still largely voluntary, a handful of EDM producers have turned themselves into ad-hoc auditors of what counts as human-made music.
stories.article_excerpt: Max Harris listens for the hiss. The EDM producer has spent months turning his feed into an informal forensics desk.

pull_quote.text: If they can do it with major artists like her, they can do it with you, me, and everyone else.
pull_quote.role: Producer and DJ, former major-label mixing engineer

stories.headline: DeepMind Cyclone Model Buys Forecasters a Full Extra Day, Nature Study Finds
stories.key_takeaway: A Nature study shows Google DeepMind WeatherNext Cyclones beats leading physics-based models on cyclone track, intensity and wind structure by more than 24 hours of lead time, and the model is now open source.
stories.article_excerpt: Google DeepMind published in Nature the peer-reviewed case for a model that had already been in operational use.

pull_quote.text: Tropical storms and hurricanes can change very quickly in terms of their structure and their intensity, which makes them more challenging to predict than other types of weather systems.

data_points.label: Five-day track error vs 370 km for ENS

stories.headline: LLMjacking Evolves: Attackers Are Now Using Stolen AI Compute to Build Offensive Agents
stories.key_takeaway: Sysdig captured an attacker using an internet-exposed, unauthenticated model server as the reasoning engine for a multi-stage automated attack framework, marking a shift from reselling stolen inference to building offensive capability with it.
stories.article_excerpt: A residential broadband connection began sending requests to an AI model server that should never have been reachable.

pull_quote.text: The cost of running offensive AI tooling is collapsing toward zero for any actor willing to steal someone else compute.

data_points.label: Modeled cost of one hijacked account
Rise in AI service credential theft

stories.headline: Multi-Agent Science Moves From Demo to Method, and the Bottleneck Moves to Verification
stories.key_takeaway: Three multi-agent discovery systems reached peer-reviewed publication in Nature in 2026, but what they demonstrably automated is hypothesis generation and literature synthesis, not experimental validation, which is where the real bottleneck now sits.
stories.article_excerpt: The claim that AI can do science stopped being a press release in 2026 and became a citation.

pull_quote.text: a huge leap, a kind of proof-by-example fallacy that is highly non-scientific
pull_quote.role: Machine learning researcher, University of Toronto

data_points.label: AI-agent papers accepted in shadow review

stories.headline: Sony Music and Warner Chappell Sue Anthropic, Alleging Piracy at the Root of Claude Training Set
stories.key_takeaway: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell have sued Anthropic in the Northern District of California, shifting the music industry legal attack from whether AI training is fair use to how the training corpus was acquired.
stories.article_excerpt: The music industry has spent nearly three years arguing that training an AI model on copyrighted songs is itself infringement. This suit changes the question.

pull_quote.text: Defendants Anthropic and its founders have conducted a brazen campaign of illegally torrenting, scraping, and downloading copyrighted works on a massive scale.
pull_quote.attribution: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music

stories.headline: The Fed Starts Treating AI as a Factor of Production
stories.key_takeaway: Warsh has put AI into the Fed framework as a potential new factor of production, but the capex boom it has produced is currently indistinguishable from a productivity boom in the data, leaving monetary policy exposed on both sides.
stories.article_excerpt: On his 100th day in the job, Kevin Warsh spent the opening of his Jackson Hole keynote on artificial intelligence.

pull_quote.text: We recognize that AI is a new variable, potentially a new factor of production, that will have consequences for both the economy and the conduct of monetary policy.

data_points.label: US GDP spent on AI data centres, Q1 2026

stories.headline: Poland Asks Brussels to Fine Meta 250M Euro Over Scam Ads; Meta Answers With an AI Detector
stories.key_takeaway: Poland DSA referral pushed Meta to ship an upgraded AI impersonation detector and full financial-advertiser verification within 48 hours, showing regulators can convert enforcement threats into product specifications without ever issuing a fine.
stories.article_excerpt: Poland cybersecurity agency ran a test on Meta. CERT Polska flagged 122 advertisements it had classified as fraudulent.

pull_quote.text: Inaction and ineffectiveness in combating harmful advertisements and fraudulent content targeting Poles will not be tolerated. I expect the European Commission to conduct the proceedings swiftly.
pull_quote.role: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Digital Affairs, Poland

data_points.label: CERT Polska reports Meta declined to remove

stories.headline: Siemens CEO to Brussels: Your Rulemaking Takes Two Years, AI Ships Eight Generations
stories.key_takeaway: Siemens CEO Roland Busch says EU lawmaking moves six to eight AI model generations too slowly, reigniting a fight over whether the June 2026 simplification package restored competitiveness or weakened safeguards before they ever applied.
stories.article_excerpt: Roland Busch did not measure Europe regulatory lag in months. He measured it in model generations.

pull_quote.text: We must not slow the development pace of AI technology through regulation.

stories.headline: xAI v. Colorado: The First Real Test of Who Governs American AI
stories.key_takeaway: The xAI federal suit against Colorado AI Act, joined by the Justice Department and now paused by court order while the state rewrites the law, is the first real test of whether states retain authority to regulate AI.
stories.article_excerpt: xAI is asking a federal judge in Denver to answer a question no court has squarely resolved: who gets to govern AI.

pull_quote.text: SB 205 is about consequential decisions, not about freedom of speech.
pull_quote.role: Colorado State Representative and lead sponsor of SB 24-205
